title: Public readiness and automatic controller setup
summary: Added first-run readiness inspection and transactional vJoy/HidHide setup so the surrounding Windows controller stack could be repaired from inside the app.
statusNote: Do not use. The initial Setup & Verification experience could interrupt healthy startup, misclassify a vJoy device already owned by HOTAS BF6, provide unclear verification progress, and fail automatic-repair flows. v1.9.1 improved verification, and v1.9.2 completed the corrective Automatic Repair transaction work.
highlights: First-run Controller Setup wizard and persistent Settings entry for Detect → Explain → Fix → Verify → Ready.
Capability planner computes required virtual axes, buttons, and native POV capacity from profiles and Automation.
vJoyConfig integration snapshots Device 1, proposes narrow changes, verifies results, and supports rollback.
HidHideCLI integration allowlists HOTAS BF6 before hiding only the selected physical device and preserves unrelated configuration.
Mapping is explicitly neutralized before setup changes.
Added normal development CI, MIT licensing, third-party notices, hardware compatibility documentation, and conservative BF6/anticheat guidance.

title: HOTAS setup verification stabilization
summary: Stabilized and polished the v1.9 controller-readiness experience while leaving the real-time mapper architecture unchanged.
statusNote: Do not use for automatic repair. This release fixed healthy-startup and readiness-verification problems, but its Automatic Repair confirmation/elevation path could still produce repeated administrator prompts, weak failure reporting, and unsuccessful repair transactions. v1.9.2 specifically corrects that path.
highlights: Healthy startup uses passive asynchronous readiness checking instead of an unnecessary setup interruption.
vJoy Device 1 is accepted as ready when owned by HOTAS BF6, while external ownership remains a real conflict.
Verification uses active controller-report evidence and exact HID/PnP identity captured by DirectInput.
Full verification visibly reports progress across physical HOTAS, vJoy output, and HidHide isolation checks.
Verification and scoped automatic repairs restore the prior Mapping On/Off choice.
Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun use the same setup/verification behavior and terminology.

title: Automatic HOTAS Repair transaction stabilization
summary: Corrected the Automatic HOTAS Repair path so one approved repair uses one elevation boundary, preserves transactional rollback and diagnostics, and verifies the result clearly.
statusNote: Current recommended published release. Use this instead of v1.9.0 or v1.9.1.
highlights: Automatic repair confirmation is a shared themed in-app overlay across Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun and shows the exact planned changes before elevation.
One confirmed repair crosses one elevation boundary instead of launching separate elevated HidHide/vJoy commands.
Partial work rolls back within the same approved transaction where safe.
Per-operation completion state, exit code, stdout, and stderr are retained for diagnostics and concise user-facing failures.
Administrator denial is reported as cancellation rather than a technical failure.
Successful commands are followed by bounded full verification; inconclusive verification is reported as Attention rather than Repair Failed.
HidHide repair uses the normalized exact selected HID instance and preserves unrelated hidden-device/application rules.
Automatic repair restores the Mapping On/Off state that existed before the transaction, including safe failure/cancellation paths.
